mbm-2926.clue: My first bowling trophy is made of toast.
mbm-2926.quote: The first morning after I bowled three strikes, my little sister cut three tiny crosses in my breakfast toast. I took a photo and ate the trophy with marmalade.

mbm-2927.clue: My plant pot has a cardigan.
mbm-2927.quote: I used the last of my winter wool to crochet around a cracked plant pot. The buttons don't undo and the plant doesn't mind. In summer it grows flowers the same orange as the sleeves.

mbm-2928.clue: The night train runs along the binding.
mbm-2928.quote: I pieced a quilt from my children's old pajamas. A little train printed on one cuff runs all the way to the edge. I sewed two black stitches at the end so it has a station to sleep in.

mbm-2929.clue: One bird in my journal is all footprints.
mbm-2929.quote: I found its tracks across the frost and followed them to the hedge. The bird had already gone. I drew the whole walk and left a little gap where the wings must have opened.

mbm-2930.clue: My antenna points toward the kettle.
mbm-2930.quote: My radio is on the other side of the kitchen wall. When I make a long-distance contact I can hear Dad setting out two mugs. He always wants the full story while the tea is hot.

mbm-2931.clue: I keep one landscape the color of tomato soup.
mbm-2931.quote: I photographed a foggy hillside through the red wrapper from a sweet. The whole hill turned warm as a stove. That print lives by the window for days when the sky forgets its colors.

mbm-2932.clue: Our quilt has a working sundial.
mbm-2932.quote: I stitched a black cat and its long blue shadow across the picnic blanket. My nephew stands the basket handle up on the cat's ears to match the shadow. Lunch is easy to tell apart from teatime.

mbm-2933.clue: I won the prize for cleanest ears.
mbm-2933.quote: Our pie contest gave us enormous paper bibs, but nobody mentioned ears. I tucked mine under my cap. The judge shook my hand and said I'd solved a problem he hadn't considered.

mbm-2934.clue: We keep the penguin pajamas for documentaries.
mbm-2934.quote: My cousin wore tuxedo-pattern pajamas for a nature show and blended beautifully with the penguins. Now he introduces each documentary with a bow from the sofa. He won't do the news.

mbm-2935.clue: My call log starts with coffee rings.
mbm-2935.quote: The first ham contact I made was so surprising that I set my mug down on my open notebook. I write each new year's first call inside a penciled circle. Every year gets a full cup.

mbm-2936.clue: I sketch the handrails between galleries.
mbm-2936.quote: The museum has one old brass rail worn smooth where school groups turn the corner. I drew the rail with a river of empty space round it. My teacher could tell exactly which staircase it was.

mbm-2937.clue: I can smell the sunshine from the bottom of the stairs.
mbm-2937.quote: My brother grows tomatoes beside the roof chairs. I rub one leaf between my fingers when I settle down to catch the sun. One gray afternoon he left a leaf on my pillow. I'd have known our roof with my eyes shut.

mbm-2938.clue: I collect keys that open nothing I own.
mbm-2938.quote: At street markets I look for funny old keys. I turned three into a little wind chime. On a windy night it sounds like somebody coming home from everywhere at once.

mbm-2939.clue: My tent has a tiny town square.
mbm-2939.quote: We put our mugs handle to handle in the tent porch. Each handle is a different street. My nephew names the meeting place Spoon Square and calls everyone there for breakfast.

mbm-2940.clue: I finally found a use for my lopsided circle.
mbm-2940.quote: My teacher asked us to draw the path of our hands after each form. I always drew one lopsided circle. A classmate put mine under the glass on the desk with a little paper tail and made it a fish. Nobody was afraid to show their drawing after that.

mbm-2941.clue: My flower goes away with a sneeze.
mbm-2941.quote: I fold a little paper flower into a silk handkerchief and have a friend pretend to sneeze. Open the silk and colored petals tumble out. My aunt sneezed for real and stole the whole show.

mbm-2942.clue: Our club takes attendance in crayon.
mbm-2942.quote: Everyone draws a little face on a sheet before we watch a cartoon. At the end we draw the expression on our face after the last scene. You can tell which weeks we picked comedies from the crooked grins.

mbm-2943.clue: My needle book has a handle.
mbm-2943.quote: I made the cover from a piece of red leather and stitched two tiny handles on top. My grandma called it a suitcase for needles. Its first journey was across the room to fix her cuff.

mbm-2944.clue: My uncle measures with his old guitar string.
mbm-2944.quote: We use a piece of blue guitar string to judge the close bocce shots. When it goes taut my uncle plucks one note and declares the winner. Ties sound especially cheerful.

mbm-2945.clue: I went looking for a vase and found a shoe.
mbm-2945.quote: At the flea market I found a ceramic boot with a hole in the heel. I put a little plant in it. Every time it needs water I get to polish one extremely shiny toe.

mbm-2946.clue: The left tunnel remembers my birthday.
mbm-2946.quote: Our mini-golf course has two dark tunnels in the mountain. I made a hole in one through the left one on my birthday. Each year I give it a turn before I try the sensible route.

mbm-2947.clue: My training diary has one square of denim.
mbm-2947.quote: I started lifting when I could barely carry my dad's tool bag. He cut a square from its old handle wrap for the cover of my log. The bag feels lighter and that square hasn't changed a bit.

mbm-2948.clue: My practice partner owns the loudest socks.
mbm-2948.quote: We train on padded mats in a chilly community room. My friend pulls bright socks on between rounds and tells me to look for them on my next turn. Two orange heels are harder to miss than a shouted correction.

mbm-2949.clue: My dad's favorite part is the bit nobody sees.
mbm-2949.quote: My first big quilt got too heavy to turn on my own. Dad built two wooden rollers for my worktable. I stitched a pair of small brown hands into the backing right where he helped me roll the last row. He checks them every time we wash it.

mbm-2950.clue: I give the flashlight to whoever is coldest.
mbm-2950.quote: At pajama cartoon night the corner lamp broke, so my nephew held a flashlight under his chin to introduce the show. That pale spooky face introduced a very cheerful duck. Now the coldest person gets the warm blanket and the flashlight for opening duties.
